Graeme Cremer to Ziaur Rahman Sharifi, out Caught by Brian Bennett!! Zimbabwe have done it. Mad scenes here at Sharjah. Stunned silence in the Afghanistan dug out. Naseer Khan Maroofkhil cannot watch it. Soon after the catch, he fell backwards in grief struggling to process what he just saw. A lovely teasing legbreak wide of off stump and drew Ziaur Rahman Sharifi into a big forward defensive stride. The edge has been found and the Zimbabwean skipper takes an excellent low catch at second slip. They win by 57 runs and take the series 1-0. Rahmat has a wry smile while the dug out stares in disbelief. Bowling coach Courtney Walsh rushes out to the centre with relief written all over his face. Bennett collects a stump as a souvenir as he tastes his first ever Test win as captain. He completed the catch, threw his cap in the air and ran across the infield with great exuberance. 17:19 local, 13:19 GMT, 18:49 IST: A hard-earned victory for Zimbabwe, but they were made to work right till the dying moments! After declaring with a lead of 417 yesterday, they seemed to have one foot in the door, needing just five wickets at the start of the day. Afghanistan, however, showed tremendous grit and character to drag the contest into the final 15 minutes. They lost Ikram Alikhil early, but Naseer Khan Maroofkhil produced an extraordinary fightback, first building a crucial 114-run stand for the seventh wicket with Zazai and then carrying on despite taking several blows to the body, battling a hamstring issue and looking completely drained towards the final session. He refused to give in, though, and went on to register a magnificent maiden Test century.

Zimbabwe, meanwhile, had their share of frustration, spilling at least four catches, three of them off Blessing Muzarabani. The big man kept charging in and peppering the batters with short balls, and his persistence finally paid off three overs after the tea break when he broke the stubborn partnership. But Afghanistan weren't done just yet, and Naseer kept fighting with whatever little he had left in the tank. Eventually, with the light fading and the clock ticking down, Sharifi edged one to slip off Cremer. Had that wicket not come, the umpires might well have called it a draw within the next couple of overs as the light continued to deteriorate. What a finish!

Bennett collects the trophy and hoists it aloft to a massive cheer. His teammates take turns lifting the silverware as the support staff join in, posing for the cameras and soaking in the moment. What a fitting way to celebrate a memorable series triumph, especially with head coach Justin Sammons having announced his decision to step down just two days ago. Sammons has expressed his desire to return home to South Africa to spend more time with his family. A lovely moment for the Zimbabwe camp and a fitting send-off for their departing coach!

All in all, a superb Test match and a thoroughly deserved series win for Zimbabwe, who dominated large phases of the contest. After a lifeless draw in the opener, this was exactly the kind of result neutral fans would have hoped for. Brendan Taylor laid the foundation with a magnificent first-innings knock, but the final two days belonged to Muzarabani, who showed immense character with both bat and ball. And a special mention for Naseer Khan Maroofkhil, whose nine-wicket haul along with a courageous maiden century on debut nearly pulled off something extraordinary for Afghanistan. Zimbabwe eventually prevailed by a narrow margin in the final session to seal the series 1-0. Right, that is all we have from Zimbabwe's tour of the UAE. We hope you had great fun following every single game. Until next time, cheers and goodbye from all of us down here...
